messages:
kevin: Pager fired ~01:30 UTC — multiple 500s from /v1/generate on dedicated-usw2 pool. Seeing p95 token latency spike + some OOM-ish logs. anyone on night?

incident-bot: [ALERT] 3 pages in last 6m for service: inference-dedicated-usw2 (sev-2). Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/ooms

sasha: I'm primary for the shift, on it. grabbing logs and tailing batcher.

kevin: thx. can you check batcher queue & pod restarts? looks like memory climbs steady.

sasha: quick repro logs: `Batcher: queue_size=320, mem_rss=47Gi, evictions=12`

sasha: checked k8s — one replica restarted 2x in the last 10m. node shows GPU memory pressure.

maria: I'm secondary, can take customer comms and ticket triage. which customers hit it?

jonathan: I see two high-traffic customers: cust-acme and cust-ozon. cust-acme saw 502s for ~3min, cust-ozon has retries and elevated latencies. created tickets #INC-2319 and #INC-2320.

kevin: suggestion: scale pool down to 2 smaller replicas then drain the noisy node, or fallback route some traffic to hosted compute (lower perf) for affected accounts.

sasha: trying a rolling restart on the batcher pods now. command: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher -n inference-dedicated-usw2```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by sasha — rollout restart started: deployment/batcher (seen 3 pods terminate/replace).

sasha: restart in progress, monitoring memory. if that doesn't cut it, I'll trigger autoscale to 4 replicas temporarily: ```kubectl scale deployment/batcher --replicas=4 -n inference-dedicated-usw2```

kevin: for safety add a routing policy to divert traffic for cust-acme and cust-ozon to fallback-usw2 via temporary policy: `/routing/policies/fallback-usw2` (ops-console).

maria: on tickets: letting cust-acme know we saw elevated 502s, we applied a restart and are monitoring. asking if they saw lost requests. cust-ozon notified as "degraded" and offered retry guidance.

sasha: restart completed, mem_rss dropped to ~12Gi and queue_size back to ~40. no further restarts.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] error rate reduced to baseline in the last 4m. pages: 0. Recommended follow-up: run heap dump + postmortem if recurrence.

kevin: good. still propose we keep temporary routing policy in place for the next 30m while we watch. I'll file a short postmortem and link to the logs: https://logs.redwood/internal/query?inc=2171509876

maria: updated tickets #INC-2319, #INC-2320 with timeline and mitigation steps. asked product ops to review model memory settings for the affected variant.

sasha: outstanding actions for next shift: 1) verify no mem leak in model binary (run memcheck job), 2) validate autoscale config doesn't overcommit GPU memory, 3) if we see >2 restarts in 1h trigger redeploy to older model variant. runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/memory-spike (section: "batcher restart + fallback routing").

kevin: handing over primary to maria at 02:15 UTC. i'm off at 02:20. @maria you'll be primary, @jonathan secondary. escalation path unchanged.

maria: taking primary. I'll keep the routing policy and monitor for 1h, will escalate to infra if we see repeat OOMs.

jonathan: ack. I'll watch dashboards and handle any customer callbacks.

kevin: final notes: incident severity lowered to sev-3 pending postmortem. no known data loss. next steps: postmortem draft in #postmortems, assign to infra+ml-team.

maria: thanks team. leaving notes in the handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/hand-offs/2171509876. primary/secondary coverage logged. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: [CLOSEABLE] alert stable. Mark for follow-up: owner=maria, ticket=INC-2319/2320, postmortem=PM-4621
